# Step 2.177: a scorekeeper undoes a final score they typed themselves

Builder 1, 2026-11-24. Branch `lane/2.177-undo-final`, six commits.

## What exists

- **Migration 0026** (`0026_who_recorded_a_result.sql`, needs renumbering at landing): `games.finalized_by`, the account that decided a game by hand, written with every result change in `update-game-result.ts`, from `decidedBy` on `GameResultChange` (set by `decide-game.ts`: a final score, box score, forfeit or imported score). Read inside the database by `find-game-decided-by.ts`, which is `LiveGamesStore.decidedBy`. `npm run db:types` has been run.
- **The rule**: `own-result-window.ts` (core/games), used by two new commands, both needing `games.score`: `games.reopen_own_result` and the read `games.read_own_result_offer`. People who may correct games can reopen at any time. Otherwise only the person who recorded the result, within `games.scorekeeperReopenMinutes`, timed by the database clock. A refusal gives `{ code, whoCan: 'games.correct', recordedBy }`. A double tap gives one correction and one activity entry, because the version check refuses the second tap (T-348).
- **The screen**: `reopen-view.ts` has a third door, `own`. `read-reopen-views.ts` (the games list) and `box-score-page.tsx` (the game's page) read the own offer for people who may not correct games. `run-box-score-action.ts` sends door `own` to `reopenOwnResult`. New messages: `admin.games.reopenUntilOwn` and three `admin.boxScore.error.*`, plus activity words.
- **Tests**: `reopen-own-result.test.ts` (own entry inside, at exactly 30 minutes, and one second after; setting 0 and 60; another person's entry and none; forfeit; owner and scheduler; editor and no account; double tap; not decided; overturned; reason). `read-own-result-offer.test.ts`. Rows in `role-matrix.test.ts`, and three isolation cases in `games-cases.test-helper.ts`. Web: `reopen-view.test.ts` and `reopen-line.test.ts`. The new read is entered in `activity-messages.test.ts`.
- **Decisions pending**: T-347 (the column and the second door), T-348 (double tap), S-94 (a box score counts, decided for you). P7 §5.5 is corrected.

## Run and passed

core games (436 tests), database isolation and role matrix (609 tests, three new cases), migrations and schema (422), games-area, site, the stand-in world agreeing with the database, activity messages, `npm run test:web` (270 checks), `node --test tests/pending-decisions.test.mjs`, `npm run check`, `npm run typecheck`.

## Left (exactly)

1. The browser test of the done test, `tests/browser/scorekeeper-own-correction-test.mjs`, entered in `scripts/web-browser-chain.mjs`. In it: a scorekeeper saves a wrong final score, taps "Correct this result", gives a reason and saves the right score. After the minutes, and for a score someone else typed, they read who can. A double tap gives one correction and one activity entry. Then the pictures.
2. The harmful-text browser test opens no new route or field (the reason field already exists). Check it in that run.
3. The tracked-game branch (`not-recorded-by-hand`) has no unit test of its own yet.

## What I distrust

- The stand-in world keeps who recorded a result in `s.deciders`, a field outside its game rows. Its seed does not fill it, so seeded final games read as recorded by nobody.
- The games list now makes one more read for each decided game, for people who may not correct games.

## Builder 2 (closing the step)

Builder 2, 2026-11-24. Three more commits on the lane branch; `build/stage-1` merged in (already up to date).

- **One read for the whole games list (T-349, pending).** `games.read_own_result_offers` (core, a read) gives each listed game's own window from one statement, `list-hand-results.ts` (`LiveGamesStore.handResults`, league-fenced), plus one read of the league's minutes. `read-reopen-views.ts` asks it once, for the games of people who may not correct games. `own-result-window.ts` keeps one rule for both reads (`scorekeeperWindow`). `read-own-result-offers.test.ts` counts the reads (one for four games, none for an empty list). There is a role row (anyone who scores somewhere, as for `games.list_my_games`), two isolation cases, and an entry in `activity-messages.test.ts`.
- **A game its tracker ended:** unit tests for `not-recorded-by-hand`, for one game and for a list.
- **The stand-in world's seed:** final scores and forfeits typed by hand are recorded by the leagues' owner (`recorderAccountId`). Games with plays are recorded by nobody.
- **Browser test `tests/browser/own-result-test.mjs`** (13 checks). The chain finds it by its name; it is not a helper. The clock starts at noon (`LOCAL_NOW`), so the screen reads "until 12:30 PM". A double tap gives one activity entry, counted in the owner's activity log. The public page shows the right score. For a score the owner typed and a forfeit a scheduler recorded, the scorekeeper reads who can. A reopen posted with scripts off (their own form, pointed at the other game) is refused and changes nothing. With the minutes set to 1, the scorekeeper reads within 90 s that their time is over. Pictures at 320, 390, 768 and 1280 in `.local/pictures`; three were looked at and none was broken.
- **Checks that failed when broken by hand:** the list's offer read and the window's time check, broken together. "Until" and "time over" both failed. Product diff empty after restoring.

### Run and passed

`npm run check`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:web` (270), pending decisions (11). Vitest of core games, database isolation, role matrix, schema, web games-area, server and site: 185 files, 2692 tests. Browser tests that passed: own-result, harmful-text (2100), games-area, corrected-mark, ask-first, after-midnight, activity-log, draft-put-back, later-games, saves-keep.

### Left, and what I distrust

- The rest of the browser chain (about 56 tests) was not run; the command budget ran out. `fence-filter-check.mjs` was not run on `list-hand-results.ts`.
- Each activity entry keeps no reason, for the admin's reopen as well as this one; the reason is kept with the correction. So the double tap's one correction is proven by the unit test, not in the browser.
- A scorekeeper cannot record a forfeit (`games.results`), so the own door for a forfeit is reached only by a role that can record forfeits but not correct games.
- The two "broken by hand" checks failed together, in one build.
